evals.expected_output: A thorough Rust API design review identifying naming violations, getter conventions, error handling, public field exposure, missing trait implementations, and parameter types. Findings should reference specific guideline identifiers.
expectations: Identifies naming violation: Db_Connection should be DbConnection (C-CASE)
Identifies getter naming: get_timeout should be timeout() (C-GETTER)
Identifies missing Result return types — connect and run_query should return Result, not String/panic (M-PANIC-IS-STOP, C-GOOD-ERR)
Identifies public fields that should be private with accessors (C-STRUCT-PRIVATE)
Identifies missing common trait implementations — at minimum Debug on DbConnection (C-COMMON-TRAITS / M-PUBLIC-DEBUG)
Identifies that DbError should implement std::error::Error (C-GOOD-ERR)
Identifies query: String should accept &str or impl AsRef<str> to avoid unnecessary allocation (C-GENERIC / M-IMPL-ASREF)

evals.expected_output: A thorough review identifying static mut unsoundness, unwrap abuse, unsafe misuse, panicking index access, and parameter type issues. Findings should reference specific guideline identifiers and include code fixes.
expectations: Identifies static mut CACHE as unsound — should use OnceLock, Mutex, or similar (M-AVOID-STATICS, M-UNSOUND)
Identifies excessive .unwrap() calls — should return Result with proper error types (M-PANIC-IS-STOP)
Identifies unsafe { from_utf8_unchecked } with untrusted input — should use from_utf8 (M-UNSAFE)
Identifies index access on parts[0]/parts[1] can panic on malformed input (M-PANIC-IS-STOP)
Identifies path: String should accept impl AsRef<Path> (M-IMPL-ASREF / C-GENERIC)
References specific guideline identifiers (M-prefixed or C-prefixed codes) in the review
Provides concrete code fixes, not just descriptions of problems

evals.prompt: I'm designing a Rust library crate for HTTP client configuration. Users need to configure: base URL, timeout (seconds), max retries, optional auth token, optional proxy URL, and custom headers. What Rust best practices should I follow for the public API design?
evals.expected_output: Comprehensive Rust API design guidance covering builder pattern, strong types, common traits, documentation, Send/Sync, error handling, and specific guideline references.
expectations: Recommends the builder pattern for complex construction (M-INIT-BUILDER / C-BUILDER)
Recommends strong types over primitives — e.g. Duration instead of u64 for timeout, newtype for URL (M-STRONG-TYPES / C-NEWTYPE / C-CUSTOM-TYPE)
Recommends implementing common traits: Debug, Clone, Default (C-COMMON-TRAITS / M-PUBLIC-DEBUG)
Covers documentation requirements: crate-level docs, examples, Errors/Panics sections (C-CRATE-DOC / C-EXAMPLE / C-FAILURE / M-FIRST-DOC-SENTENCE)
Recommends Send + Sync for async runtime compatibility (M-TYPES-SEND / C-SEND-SYNC)
Addresses error handling — custom error type implementing std::error::Error (C-GOOD-ERR / M-ERRORS-CANONICAL-STRUCTS)
References specific guideline identifiers (M-prefixed or C-prefixed codes)
